# nbzinbPate

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/brandonp8/nbzinbPate/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/brandonp8/nbzinbPate/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**nbzinbPate** fits

* **negative binomial (NB2) regression** with `nbreg()`, comparable to
  `MASS::glm.nb()`, and
* **zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression** with `zinbreg()`,
  comparable to `pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin")`,

with all of the estimation implemented from scratch. No general-purpose
optimizer (`optim()`, `nlm()`, ...) and no GLM fitter (`glm()`, `lm()`, ...)
is used:

* **NB**: iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients
  with \(\theta\) fixed, alternated with Newton-Raphson for \(\log\theta\)
  with the coefficients fixed.
* **ZINB**: an EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability
  that each zero is a structural zero. The M-step fits a fractional-response
  logistic regression for the zero model and a weighted NB regression for the
  count model, both by IRLS.
* **Standard errors**: \((X^\top \hat W X)^{-1}\) and
  \(\{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}\) for NB. For ZINB, the inverse observed
  information, computed from an **analytic** Hessian of the observed-data
  log-likelihood with respect to \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\).

This package was written for the STA 651 Module 2 final project (Fall 2026).

**Website:** <https://brandonp8.github.io/nbzinbPate/>, with the function
reference and the [project report](https://brandonp8.github.io/nbzinbPate/articles/report.html)
(also available as a PDF:
[`report/report.pdf`](https://github.com/brandonp8/nbzinbPate/blob/master/report/report.pdf)).

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("brandonp8/nbzinbPate")
```

The package only depends on base R (`stats`). The reference packages `MASS`,
`pscl`, `AER` and `numDeriv` are needed only to run the tests.

## Example

The `bioChemists` data (from **pscl**) record the number of articles published
by 915 biochemistry PhD students.

```{r nb}
library(nbzinbPate)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
m_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(m_nb)
```

```{r zinb}
# Zero-inflated NB: count model before "|", zero-inflation model after it
m_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | kid5 + ment,
                  data = bioChemists)
summary(m_zinb)
```

The usual methods work: `coef()`, `vcov()`, `logLik()`, `AIC()`, `BIC()`,
`fitted()`, `residuals()`, `nobs()`, and `predict()`, including
`predict(m_zinb, newdata, type = "response" / "count" / "zero")`.

```{r methods}
AIC(m_nb, m_zinb)
predict(m_zinb, newdata = data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married",
                                     kid5 = 0, phd = 3, ment = c(0, 10, 40)),
        type = "zero")
```

## Agreement with the reference implementations

On `bioChemists` and `AER::NMES1988`, the estimates match `MASS::glm.nb()` and
`pscl::zeroinfl()` far more closely than the project tolerances require.

* **NB vs `glm.nb()`**: the coefficients, their standard errors, \(\theta\)
  and the log-likelihood agree to about 1e-10. SE(\(\theta\)) agrees to about
  1e-6, because `glm.nb()` evaluates it at the second-to-last Newton step for
  \(\theta\).
* **ZINB vs `zeroinfl()`**: the coefficients, standard errors and
  \(\log\theta\) agree to about 1e-5 or better, and the log-likelihood to
  about 1e-9.

The package tests (`tests/testthat/`) check this agreement automatically.
